fieldsRead.text: This English-taught TU/e degree studies buildings and cities through design, engineering, environmental performance and the needs of their users. The Architectural Urban Design and Engineering pathway develops architectural and urban design through projects, history, technology and research.
The published project credits and elective requirements conflict, so a complete degree pathway and UCR comparison cannot yet be confirmed. This does not establish that UCR has no relevant programme.

The supported components shown total 130 EC: 60 in year 1, 45 in year 2 and 25 in year 3. The multidisciplinary project and elective space are omitted because their published credit requirements conflict. This is an incomplete degree pathway; a complete UCR comparison awaits clarification.
One first-year project choice is shown. The later AUDE route requires its own subject and project courses; other tracks are not combined into this pathway.

Entry normally requires at least 120 EC, all compulsory first-year components, all second-year project-line projects and all multidisciplinary projects. The multidisciplinary project must be completed first.

The first-year study-advice threshold is normally 45 of 60 EC. Personal and professional development is embedded in credited courses; five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities with a total value of seven are additional non-credit requirements.
